Considering my priority ranks, I have the highest priority at schools w and y (rank 1), and a lower priority at schools x and z (rank 2). This means that at schools w and y, I am more likely to be accepted because I am the top priority. However, z offers the highest value, so I should attempt to get into z first despite the lower priority, because if I am accepted there, it maximizes my value.

If I am rejected from z, I can still propose to w and y, where I have the highest priority, making it very likely that I will be accepted at one of them. Since w and y have the same value, I will rank w ahead of y due to no particular reason to prefer one over the other besides perhaps a slight personal preference or logistical convenience.

Finally, x is the least valuable and I have a lower priority there, so it should be ranked last.

Thus, my strategy is to aim for the highest value school first, then secure a spot at a high-priority school if rejected.
